scope: Shared Web/Android memory selection and resource-specific result labels
Selected-only resolutions use the Server resourceSection and current version
Authenticated source history uses the recorded local resource and fixed batch target
Identity, scope and permission changes discard stale or private history
Private instructions and summaries remain personal; family facts/topics retain shared destinations

verification.check: TypeScript dependency graph for seven changed entrypoints using the existing frontend config plus Node types for Node tests

verification.reason: Final cancellation regression and summary restoration contract alignment

retainedFailures: Owner/client and component checks initially failed before the new connections existed.
The initial scoped typecheck used frontend-only ambient types for Node tests and returned 30 diagnostics; adding the existing Node types resolved these without changing project configuration.
Interrupting a pending history read through the owner API left loading true. The same scenario was added to the owner check and passed after cancellation cleared loading.

The initial UI excluded summary restoration even when the Server offered it. Removed that extra restriction; the final regression verifies only the selected summary is submitted with the Server-provided target and expected version.

review.independent: Read-only review found no definite P1/P2 or required minor before the final main-model contract alignment.
review.main: Checked actual shared components, owner/client binding, verification output and the Server resolution contract.

limitations: The component check runs the actual shared components with synthetic React/native primitives; it is not browser or device evidence.
Source history is read-only, not a current/source body comparison.
Other import domains and the remaining full handover acceptance are still incomplete.
